name: Newcastle-under-Lyme

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: only the national mandatory licence for HMOs with five or more people from two or more households. The council has proposed planning controls (an Article 4 direction) on new small HMOs in a designated area.
licensing.fee: £750 for an HMO licence of up to five bedrooms, plus £11 for each extra bedroom

privateRentedShare.text: 14.5% of households rent privately (Census 2021), up from 10.5% in 2011

councilTax.text: £2,334.25 average Band D (2026/27), including Staffordshire County Council, police, fire and average parish precepts

housing: Newcastle-under-Lyme is a market town next to Stoke-on-Trent with former mining villages such as Silverdale, Audley and Kidsgrove and rural villages to the west. About one in seven households rent privately, with student lets serving Keele University and Victorian terraces near the town centre. Much of the rest is post-war and inter-war housing on estates around the town.
checkinTips: Student houses near Keele and the town centre: photograph every bedroom lock, fire doors, smoke alarms and the posted HMO licence.
Colliery-era terraces in Silverdale, Audley and Kidsgrove: note cracks in walls and around doors and windows that may come from old mine workings.
Victorian terraces in Wolstanton and May Bank: photograph the rear yard, gutters and any damp in back kitchens.
Flats over shops in the town centre: record the shared entrance, fire doors and key counts.
Rural homes in the western villages: photograph any oil tank, septic tank and outbuildings included in the let.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair or safety concerns can contact Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council's private sector housing team, which licenses HMOs and can inspect homes.
